visual_evidence: A thin, light-coloured wooden craft stick with a rounded tip is held by fingers in the lower-left to centre of the frame over a darker varnished wood surface.
A narrow, dark longitudinal split runs straight along the centre of the stick parallel to its length and grain, extending from the fingers to the rounded end.
The two sides of the split remain pressed together so the fracture surface is closed and hidden from view.
The wooden stick in the foreground is slightly out of focus compared with the sharper wood table surface behind it.
A faint transverse mark crosses the flat face of the stick near the rounded tip.
diagnosis.probable_cause: Cannot be determined from this photo because the fracture surface is hidden inside a closed split and the foreground part is slightly out of focus.
diagnosis.insufficient_reason: The crack is closed, so the fracture surface is hidden inside the split and cannot be seen, and the stick itself is slightly out of focus. Separate the split pieces (or open the crack enough to expose the interior faces) and take a sharp, close-up, well-lit photo looking directly at the fracture surface, along with a clear view of the full stick showing where load or fasteners were applied.
